rationale: A demo environment with Microsoft data supports Initiate-phase discovery and CRP sessions, and remains briefly available as build begins for troubleshooting against out-of-the-box behavior.
Each concurrent developer needs a dedicated development environment from the start of build until go-live; version control requires one server per developer.
GOLD accumulates approved configuration and code to become the seed for Production; it is deprecated shortly after go-live once the team is comfortable.
SIT validates code promotion through version control before it reaches UAT, from the first promotions early in build until go-live.
Data migration gets a dedicated environment per rollout so a corrupted test run can be restored without disrupting the wider project; it stays available through cutover reconciliation.
The main functional sandbox: configuration and modeling during build, acceptance and regression testing through Prepare, and the pre-production staging environment after go-live.
Performance testing runs in a production-sized environment for roughly two months ending at go-live, when volumes and code are representative.
End-user training happens during Prepare on release-branch code, continuing briefly past go-live for stragglers.
Production is provisioned ahead of go-live (the PROD lead time setting) for mock go-live and cutover rehearsal, then runs for the life of the system.
A hotfix environment mirrors production from go-live onward so fixes can be built and tested without disturbing ongoing development.
